  "overall_assessment": "anomalies",
  "findings": [
    {
      "benefit": "CI",
      "years": [2021, 2023],
      "pattern": "drift",
      "direction": "increase",
      "magnitude": "build from ~0.98 baseline to peak ~1.10-1.11 A/E (roughly +0.11 to +0.13, x1.11) over 2021-2023, then reverts to ~0.98 in 2024",
      "confidence": 0.85,
      "evidence": [
        "ae_ci_by_year.csv: A/E rises smoothly 0.98(2020)->1.04(2021)->1.10(2022)->1.11(2023), then drops to 0.98(2024) — a build-up, not a single-year step",
        "Evidence pack: 3y smoothed MA climbs steadily 1.00(2019)->1.04(2020)->1.08(2021)->1.06(2022), smoothed-fit R2 0.83, 7y up run — sustained move, not a one-off",
        "Peak years Poisson z +4.1 (2022) and +4.6 (2023); line overdispersion only x2.32 so per-year null is roughly valid",
        "Excursion 2022-2023 level +0.132 (score 9.6) vs the rest; largest single-year move does not exceed net excursion, confirming gradual build",
        "2024 reversion to 0.98 means the drift is confined to a sub-window that later returns to baseline — per guidance this is still drift; reversion noted here rather than reported as a separate event",
        "Not cross-line: CROSS-LINE flags only CI (>0.08 from own baseline) in the 2021-2023 run, so this is a CI-specific movement, not a book-wide coordinated swing"
      ],
      "recommended_action": "Investigate CI experience 2021-2023: review claim mix (diagnosis/severity and case-mix shift), changes in CI definitions, claim adjudication, or underwriting during those years; test whether the expected (pricing/valuation) frequency or severity for CI was understated in 2021-2023 vs the actual trend. Confirm what drove the 2024 reversion (actual claims normalised vs expected catching up). If the build reflects a real step in claim experience, follow up on CI pricing assumptions and valuation reserves for that window."
    }
  ]
}
